verdicts.claim: SQLite defines four checkpoint modes: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE, SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL, SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART, and SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE. PASSIVE
verdicts.evidence: c3ref page lists a fifth mode, SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP (checkpoints zero frames, used only to read output parameters); PASSIVE/busy-handler half is supported: 'The busy-handler callback is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode.'

verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'This mode blocks (it invokes the busy-handler callback) until there is no database writer and all readers are reading from the most recent database snapshot.'

verdicts.claim: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE is identical to RESTART but also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to successful return.
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'works the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART with the addition that it also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return.'

verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'All calls obtain an exclusive "checkpoint" lock ... SQLITE_BUSY is returned. Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked in this case.'

verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'threshold size of 1000 pages. (The SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT compile-time option can be used to specify a different default.)'

verdicts.evidence: wal2.md: 'wal files do not grow indefinitely even if the checkpointer never has a chance to finish uninterrupted'; 'may only be accessed by versions of SQLite compiled from this branch'; HN calls it 'experimental WAL2 branch'.
